versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: Biliary tract cancers comprise intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, perihilar (Klatskin) cholangiocarcinoma, distal cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder carcinoma, each with its own 8th-edition T definitions in one file. Intrahepatic disease is staged like liver tumours (number, vascular invasion, visceral-peritoneum perforation); perihilar and distal disease by bile-duct wall invasion and vascular involvement (unilateral vs bilateral portal or hepatic artery); gallbladder by wall-layer invasion (peritoneal vs hepatic side T2a/T2b matters for prognosis). Nodal positivity is N1 (1-3 nodes) or N2 (4 or more) except perihilar/distal schemes.

t.label: Intrahepatic: solitary tumour 5 cm or smaller without vascular invasion; Gallbladder: invasion of lamina propria
Intrahepatic: solitary tumour larger than 5 cm without vascular invasion; Gallbladder: invasion of muscle layer
Gallbladder: invasion of peritoneal-side connective tissue without serosal perforation; Distal bile duct: invasion 5-12 mm beyond duct wall
Gallbladder: invasion of hepatic-side connective tissue without liver invasion; Perihilar: beyond duct wall into surrounding fat
Intrahepatic: solitary tumour with intrahepatic vascular invasion, or multiple tumours with or without vascular invasion

Intrahepatic: tumour perforating the visceral peritoneum; Perihilar: unilateral portal vein or hepatic artery invasion; Distal: invasion beyond duct wall over 12 mm; Gallbladder: serosal perforation and/or direct liver or single extrahepatic organ invasion

Intrahepatic: direct invasion of extrahepatic structures; Perihilar: main portal vein, bilateral secondary biliary radicles, or unilateral secondary radicle with contralateral vascular invasion; Distal: coeliac, SMA or common hepatic artery invasion; Gallbladder: main portal/hepatic artery invasion or two or more extrahepatic organs

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Metastasis in 1 to 3 regional lymph nodes (perihilar/distal: nodes along bile duct, portal, hepatic artery)
Metastasis in 4 or more regional lymph nodes (intrahepatic/gallbladder schemes)

stageGroups.basis: Vascular invasion or limited local spread, node negative

versions.regionalNodes: Hilar, pericholedochal, portal, hepatic artery, posterior pancreaticoduodenal and (for gallbladder/distal) anterior pancreaticoduodenal nodes. Coeliac, para-aortic and distant nodes are M1.
versions.histologicGrade: Well differentiated (G1), moderately differentiated (G2), poorly differentiated (G3); large-duct vs small-duct intrahepatic subtypes carry different biology. Gallbladder T2a (peritoneal) vs T2b (hepatic) is reported because hepatic-side tumours behave worse.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Adenocarcinoma (most cases, tubular/papillary); intraductal papillary neoplasm with associated invasion; mucinous, signet-ring and adenosquamous variants; gallbladder: biliary-type adenocarcinoma, intestinal-type, neuroendocrine carcinoma (separate system).
prognosticFactors: Anatomic subtype (intrahepatic vs perihilar vs distal vs gallbladder)
Margin status (R0 is the dominant curative factor)
IDH1 mutation and FGFR2 fusion (intrahepatic, therapeutic)
Primary sclerosing cholangitis / choledochal cyst background
